questions.question: According to OIL RIG, oxidation is:
The oxidising agent in a redox reaction is the substance that:
options: Causes oxidation of its partner by taking electrons, and is itself reduced

questions.question: When magnesium reacts with dilute acid, magnesium moves from oxidation number 0 to +2. Magnesium is therefore:
options: Oxidised, and acting as the reducing agent
Reduced, and acting as the oxidising agent
Oxidised, and acting as the oxidising agent

questions.question: In every electrochemical cell, the anode is defined as:
options: The electrode connected to the salt bridge
The electrode with the larger mass

questions.question: A galvanic (voltaic) cell is a device that converts:
options: Electrical energy into chemical energy using a power supply
Chemical energy into electrical energy through a spontaneous redox reaction

questions.question: In the zinc-copper cell, electrons flow through the external wire:
As the zinc-copper cell operates, which set of observations is correct?
options: Zinc electrode loses mass, copper electrode gains mass, the blue colour fades
Zinc electrode gains mass and the solution turns bluer

questions.question: The two-clause exam explanation of the salt bridge's function is that it:
options: Carries electrons and cools the cell
Stirs the solutions and adds reactants
Increases the voltage and stores charge
Completes the circuit and maintains electrical neutrality in both half-cells

questions.question: Standard conditions for electrode potentials are:
options: 1 mol·dm⁻³ solutions, 25 °C, gases at standard pressure
Pure solids only, in a vacuum

questions.question: The standard hydrogen electrode is assigned a potential of exactly:
options: 0 V — it is the agreed reference for the whole table

questions.question: The more NEGATIVE a half-reaction's electrode potential, the stronger:
options: The species on the left is as an oxidising agent
The pull the half-cell exerts on electrons
The species on the right is as a reducing agent

questions.question: When two half-cells are connected, the one with the HIGHER electrode potential:
options: Runs as the reduction and becomes the cathode

questions.question: In standard cell notation, the double vertical line represents:
options: A phase boundary between electrode and solution

questions.question: The emf of a standard cell is calculated as:
For the aluminium-silver cell (E° Al = −1,66 V; E° Ag = +0,80 V), the emf is:
A 'flat' battery is best described as one in which:
options: The reaction has reached equilibrium, so the emf is zero
The salt bridge has dried up

questions.question: When zinc is dropped DIRECTLY into copper sulfate solution, the energy of the reaction:
options: Is stored in the salt bridge
Escapes as heat and is wasted

questions.question: A galvanic cell produces a current by:
options: Separating the electron donor and acceptor so the transfer must pass through the external wire
Heating the solutions until they conduct
Spinning a coil in a magnetic field

questions.question: The voltage of a cell reflects:
options: How strongly the two half-cells 'want' the electron trade — the push on each electron

subtopics.title: The Bridge That Keeps the Peace

questions.question: Without a salt bridge, the anode beaker would quickly:
options: Accumulate positive charge that drags on departing electrons and stalls the cell

questions.question: The salt bridge carries current in the form of:
options: Migrating ions — negative ions toward the anode beaker, positive ions toward the cathode beaker

questions.question: In the two-storey picture of the circuit, the 'upstairs' and 'downstairs' currents are carried by:
options: Ions in the wire; electrons in the solutions
Electrons in the wire; ions in the solutions and bridge

questions.question: If the salt bridge is lifted out of a working cell, the voltmeter reading:

subtopics.title: The League Table of Electron Grabbers

questions.question: The 'reigning champion' electron grabber at the strong-oxidiser end of the table is:
Every voltage in the table is a comparison against:
options: The standard hydrogen electrode, defined as zero
The strongest metal in the cell

questions.question: When any two entries of the table are paired in a cell, the spontaneous outcome is that:
options: The higher-ranked species takes the electrons and is reduced; the lower-ranked gives and is oxidised
The lower-ranked species takes the electrons
No reaction can occur without heating

questions.question: Battery designers hunt for material pairs with a LARGE gap between their electrode potentials because the gap determines:
options: How long the salt bridge lasts
The cell's voltage — the push on every electron
